2414.body:
The prize money on "PREMIER PLAY" leans toward the smaller prizes. It is spread over ten prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $3 million. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

If you play "PREMIER PLAY" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2414.headline: Where the prize money is

2415.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Double The Money", about half are still unsold. The game is near the midpoint of its run, with two of three top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything here about "Double The Money" comes from official Virginia lottery numbers, current through October 26.
2415.headline: Tickets sold so far

2416.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "Loaded with $2,000s" have been sold. The game is past the halfway point of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

If you play "Loaded with $2,000s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

"Gold 7s" has gone over a month without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a quarter of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $577,777 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

2421.headline: No new top prize claims

2422.body:
"Platinum 7s" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of its unclaimed prize money, about two-thirds is in wins under $2,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The numbers for "Platinum 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
